arxiv-1908-04872.title: Magnetic structure and excitations of the topological semimetal YbMnBi 2
arxiv-1908-04872.creator: Jian-Rui Soh, Henrik Jacobsen, Bachir Ouladdiaf, Alexandre Ivanov, Andrea Piovano, Tim Tejsner, Zili Feng, Hongyuan Wang, Hao Su, Yanfeng Guo, Youguo Shi, Andrew T. Boothroyd
arxiv-1908-04872.description: A 2019 arXiv research paper by Jian-Rui Soh, Henrik Jacobsen, Bachir Ouladdiaf, Alexandre Ivanov, Andrea Piovano, Tim Tejsner, Zili Feng, Hongyuan Wang, Hao Su, Yanfeng Guo, Youguo Shi, Andrew T. Boothroyd. We investigated the magnetic structure and dynamics of YbMnBi 2 , with elastic and inelastic neutron scattering, to shed light on the topological nature of the charge carriers in the antiferromagnetic phase.

arxiv-2107-03299.title: Big Data Information and Nowcasting: Consumption and Investment from Bank Transactions in Turkey
arxiv-2107-03299.description: Abstract We use the aggregate information from individual-to-firm and firm-to-firm in Garanti BBVA Bank transactions to mimic domestic private demand. Particularly, we replicate the quarterly national accounts aggregate consumption and investment (gross fixed capital formation) and its bigger components (Machinery and Equipment and Construction) in real time for the case of Turkey.

arxiv-2110-06986.title: ADMM-DAD NET: a deep unfolding network for analysis compressed sensing
arxiv-2110-06986.creator: Vasiliki Kouni, Georgios Paraskevopoulos, Holger Rauhut, George C. Alexandropoulos
arxiv-2110-06986.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a new deep unfolding neural network based on the ADMM algorithm for analysis Compressed Sensing. The proposed network jointly learns a redundant analysis operator for sparsification and reconstructs the signal of interest. We compare our proposed network with a state-of-the-art unfolded ISTA decoder, that also learns an orthogonal sparsifier.

arxiv-2307-02153.title: A renormalization group improvement for thermally resummed effective potential
arxiv-2307-02153.creator: Koichi Funakubo 1, Eibun Senaha 2,3
arxiv-2307-02153.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Koichi Funakubo 1, Eibun Senaha 2,3. We propose a novel method for renormalization group improvement of thermally resummed effective potential. In our method, β \beta -functions are temperature dependent as a consequence of the divergence structure in resummed perturbation theory.

arxiv-2311-03164.title: A contract negotiation scheme for safety verification of interconnected systems
arxiv-2311-03164.creator: Xiao Tan, Antonis Papachristodoulou, Dimos V. Dimarogonas
arxiv-2311-03164.description: Abstract This paper proposes a (control) barrier function synthesis and safety verification scheme for interconnected nonlinear systems based on assume-guarantee contracts (AGC) and sum-of-squares (SOS) techniques. It is well-known that the SOS approach does not scale well for barrier function synthesis for high-dimensional systems. In this paper, we show that compositional methods like AGC can mitigate this problem.

arxiv-2401-07050.title: Countable homogeneous ordered bipartite graphs
arxiv-2401-07050.creator: J K Truss
arxiv-2401-07050.description: Abstract A classification is given of all the countable homogeneous ordered bipartite graphs 1 1 footnotetext: 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 05C60; keywords: bipartite graph, homogeneous, ordered 1 Introduction A relational structure is said to be homogeneous (also called ‘ultrahomogeneous’, as in [ 5 ] for instance) if any isomorphism between finite substructures extends to an automorphism of the whole structure.

arxiv-2507-10291.title: High Resolution Temperature-Resolved Spectroscopy of the Nitrogen Vacancy E 1 \mathrm{{}^{1}E} Singlet State Ionization Energy
arxiv-2507-10291.description: Abstract The negatively charged diamond nitrogen-vacancy ( NV − \mathrm{{NV}^{-}} ) center plays a central role in many cutting edge quantum sensing applications; despite this, much is still unknown about the energy levels in this system. The ionization energy of the E 1 \mathrm{{}^{1}E} singlet state in the NV − \mathrm{{NV}^{-}} has only recently been measured at between 2.

arxiv-2508-02219.title: CO-RFT: Efficient Fine-Tuning of Vision-Language-Action Models through Chunked Offline Reinforcement Learning
arxiv-2508-02219.creator: Dongchi Huang, Zhirui Fang, Tianle Zhang, Yihang Li, Lin Zhao, Chunhe Xia
arxiv-2508-02219.description: Abstract Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models demonstrate significant potential for developing generalized policies in real-world robotic control. This progress inspires researchers to explore fine-tuning these models with Reinforcement Learning (RL). However, fine-tuning VLA models with RL still faces challenges related to sample efficiency, compatibility with action chunking, and training stability.

arxiv-2510-17614.title: OG-Rank: Learning to Rank Fast and Slow with Uncertainty and Reward-Trend Guided Adaptive Exploration
arxiv-2510-17614.creator: Praphul Singh, Corey Barrett, Sumana Srivasta, Irfan Bulu, Amitabh Saikia, Sri Gadde, Krishnaram Kenthapadi
arxiv-2510-17614.description: Abstract Clinicians need ranking systems that work in real time and still justify their choices. Motivated by the need for a low-latency, decoder-based reranker, we present OG-Rank, a single-decoder approach that pairs a pooled first-token scoring signal with an uncertainty-gated explanation step.

arxiv-2511-05267.title: Shallow IQP circuits and graph generation
arxiv-2511-05267.creator: Oriol Balló-Gimbernat, Marcos Arroyo-Sánchez, Paula García-Molina, Adan Garriga, Fernando Vilariño
arxiv-2511-05267.description: Abstract We introduce shallow instantaneous quantum polynomial-time (IQP) circuits as generative graph models, using an edge-qubit encoding to map graphs onto quantum states. Focusing on bipartite and Erdős–Rényi distributions, we study their expressivity and robustness through simulations and large-scale experiments.

arxiv-2601-10355.title: Unlocking Implicit Experience: Synthesizing Tool-Use Trajectories from Text
arxiv-2601-10355.creator: Zhihao Xu, Rumei Li, Jiahuan Li, Rongxiang Weng, Jingang Wang, Xunliang Cai, Xiting Wang
arxiv-2601-10355.description: Abstract Enabling Large Language Models (LLMs) to effectively utilize tools in multi-turn interactions is essential for building capable autonomous agents. However, acquiring diverse and realistic multi-turn tool-use data remains a significant challenge. In this work, we propose a novel text-based paradigm.

arxiv-2601-13699.title: Quantum Encoding Framework for Leptophilic Gauge Theories
arxiv-2601-13699.creator: S O Kara
arxiv-2601-13699.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by S O Kara. We present a systematic quantum encoding framework for leptophilic extensions of the Standard Model, tailored to quantum simulation applications on near term and future quantum devices. Focusing on anomaly free U ​ ( 1 ) ℓ ′ U(1)^{\prime}_{\ell} gauge theories, we show that the leptonic charge structure admits a natural and scalable representation on qubit registers, where gauge symmetries and anomaly cancellation conditions are enforced directly at the level of quantum states.

pmc-10573051.title: Responsiveness and Minimal Important Change of the Arabic Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) in Patients with Upper Extremity Musculoskeletal Disorders
pmc-10573051.creator: Ali H Alnahdi, Philippe Gorce
pmc-10573051.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). The aim of this study was to examine the responsiveness of the Arabic Disabilities of the Arm, Shoulder and Hand (DASH) and to quantify its minimal important change (MIC) for improvement. People with upper extremity musculoskeletal problems who were receiving physical therapy were evaluated at baseline and again during a follow-up appointment, with a median time frame of 7 days between the two testing sessions (range of 6 to 72 days).

pmc-10652455.title: A comprehensive point prevalence survey of the quality and quantity of antimicrobial use in Chinese general hospitals and clinical specialties
pmc-10652455.creator: Yonghong Xiao, Xing Xin, Yunbo Chen, Qing Yan, The China PPS team
pmc-10652455.description: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a serious, worldwide public health crisis. Surveillance of antimicrobial use forms part of an essential strategy to contain AMR. We aimed to conduct a national point prevalence survey (PPS) on antimicrobial use, and to compare this data with similar international surveillance programs to provide a reference for future AMR strategy development in China.

pmc-11306041.title: Seven psychiatric traits and the risk of increased carotid intima-media thickness: a Mendelian randomization study
pmc-11306041.creator: Kewan He, Jiajun Ying, Fangkun Yang, Teng Hu, Yuewu Du
pmc-11306041.description: BackgroundNumerous observational studies have suggested an association between psychiatric traits and carotid intima-media thickness (cIMT). However, whether these associations have a causal relationship remains unknown, largely due to issues of reverse causality and potential confounders. This study aims to elucidate the potential causal role of psychiatric traits in the risk of arterial injury as measured by cIMT.

pmc-11395665.title: Perceived structural empowerment, resilience, and intent to stay among midwives and registered nurses in Saudi Arabia: a convergent parallel mixed methods study
pmc-11395665.creator: Areej Ghalib Al-Otaibi, Ahmad E Aboshaiqah, Fatimah Ali Aburshaid, Anwar Nader AlKhunaizi, Sarah Abdulaziz AlAbdalhai
pmc-11395665.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundRetaining midwives and registered nurses in the Obstetrics and Gynecology department/unit (OB/GYN) is not just a matter of organizational effectiveness and financial wellness. It’s a crucial aspect of ensuring quality healthcare delivery.

pmc-11516161.title: Effects of upper thoracic Mulligan mobilization on pain, range of motion and function in patients with mechanical neck pain: A randomized placebo-controlled trial
pmc-11516161.creator: Ramazan Cevik, Omer Osman Pala
pmc-11516161.description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the impact of Mulligan Reverse Natural Apophyseal Glides (RNAGS) applied to the upper thoracic region on pain, movement limitation, and function in individuals with mechanical neck pain.MethodsConducted between January 2021 and May 2021, the study involved 69 participants randomly assigned to a sham group, physiotherapy group, and Mulligan group.

pmc-11538635.title: RLCFormer: Automatic roadside LiDAR-Camera calibration framework with transformer
pmc-11538635.creator: Rui Tian, Xuefeng Bao, Yunli Chen, Feng Liu, Yiqiang Zhen, Yong Li
pmc-11538635.description: LiDAR-Camera fusion is pivotal for perceiving and understanding complex traffic environments, particularly valuable in autonomous driving and traffic monitoring. Traditional calibration algorithms, primarily designed for onboard sensors, are inadequate for roadside setups where sensors are positioned higher and more dispersed. To address this challenge, we introduce the RLCFormer, a Transformer-based network specifically tailored for precise calibration of roadside sensors.

pmc-11579056.title: Technical note: durable resolution of hydrocephalus after ultrasound-guided percutaneous fenestration of giant suprasellar arachnoid cyst in a neonate
pmc-11579056.creator: Michael J Stuart, Joseph Yoon, Jane McEniery, Amelia J Jardim, Craig Vonhoff
pmc-11579056.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Arachnoid cysts are relatively common, but rarely require intervention. While most arachnoid cysts in typical middle or posterior cranial fossa locations are seldom symptomatic, suprasellar cysts may become symptomatic due to the potential for ventricular outflow obstruction and hydrocephalus. Typical standard of care for the treatment of these lesions is endoscopic fenestration with third ventriculostomy, or the placement of ventriculoperitoneal or cystoperitoneal shunts.

pmc-11623946.title: ASCL1 regulates and cooperates with FOXA2 to drive terminal neuroendocrine phenotype in prostate cancer
pmc-11623946.creator: Shaghayegh Nouruzi, Takeshi Namekawa, Nakisa Tabrizian, Maxim Kobelev, Olena Sivak, Joshua M Scurll, Cassandra Jingjing Cui, Dwaipayan Ganguli, Amina Zoubeidi
pmc-11623946.description: Lineage plasticity mediates resistance to androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) and progression from adenocarcinoma to neuroendocrine prostate cancer (NEPC), a highly aggressive and poorly understood subtype. Neuronal transcription factor ASCL1 has emerged as a central regulator of the lineage plasticity driving neuroendocrine differentiation.

pmc-11657206.title: Nationwide survey on awareness of consanguinity and genetic diseases in Saudi Arabia: challenges and potential solutions to reduce the national healthcare burden
pmc-11657206.creator: Nura A. Yousef, Ashraf A. ElHarouni, Noor Ahmad Shaik, Babajan Banaganapalli, Asayil Faisal Al Ghamdi, Amani H. Galal, Turki Saad Alahmadi, Taghreed Shuaib, Deema Aljeaid, Dalal S. Alshaer, Mahmoud Almutadares, Ramu Elango
pmc-11657206.description: BackgroundConsanguineous marriage is a major contributing factor for many genetic diseases and a burden to the healthcare system and national economy due to costly long-term care. Earlier studies highlighted the significantly limited awareness of the higher prevalence of genetic disease due to consanguinity even among the educated Arabs. In Saudi Arabia, more than 50% of marriages are between first cousins.

pmc-11674999.title: Assessment of the American College of Surgeons Surgical Risk Calculator (ACS-SRC) for Prediction of Early Postoperative Complications in Patients Undergoing Cytoreductive Surgery for Ovarian Peritoneal Carcinomatosis
pmc-11674999.creator: Cedric Kabeya, Charif Khaled, Laura Polastro, Michel Moreau, Dario Bucella, Maxime Fastrez, Gabriel Liberale
pmc-11674999.description: Ovarian cancer (OC) is diagnosed at a locally advanced stage in two-thirds of cases. The first line of treatment consists of cytoreductive surgery (CRS) combined with neoadjuvant and/or adjuvant chemotherapy. However, CRS can be associated with high rates of postoperative complications (POCs), and detection of fragile patients at high risk of POCs is important.

pmc-11801078.title: Investigating the Impact of Voxel Size and Postfiltering on Quantitative Analysis of Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography: A Phantom Study
pmc-11801078.creator: Ahmed Abdel Mohymen, Hamed Ibrahim Farag, Sameh M. Reda, Ahmed Soltan Monem, Said A. Ali
pmc-11801078.description: Aim:This study aims to investigate the influence of voxel size and postfiltering on the quantification of standardized uptake value (SUV) in positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) images.Materials and Methods:National Electrical Manufacturers Association phantom with the spheres of different sizes were utilized to simulate the lesions.

pmc-11814186.title: The spatial buildup of nonlinear compression in the cochlea
pmc-11814186.creator: Kostas Kondylidis, Anna Vavakou, Marcel van der Heijden
pmc-11814186.description: In the mammalian cochlea, the transduction from vibrations to inner hair cell receptor currents is preceded by a stage of mechanical pre-processing that involves a rapid, strongly nonlinear compression. The mechanisms by which the cochlea realizes this dynamic compression are still poorly understood.

pmc-12578706.title: Multidimensional analysis reveals the potential of ACSL3 as a cancer biomarker: from pan-cancer exploration to functional validation in hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-12578706.creator: Qun Niu, Yu Mou, Yuanqian Yao, HaiJian Dong, Kaixin Wang, Zijian Zeng, Yujing Tao, Xueqing Gong, Hui Li
pmc-12578706.description: ACSL3 converts long-chain fatty acids into acyl-CoA, a key step in lipid metabolism. Since this process is linked to cancer development and progression, this study investigates the specific roles and underlying mechanisms of ACSL3 across various cancer types. We examined ACSL3 by analyzing its expression, transcriptomic variations, single-cell localization, prognostic significance, and biological roles using various databases and perspectives.

pmc-12586646.title: Redox regulation by sulfiredoxin-1: bridging cysteine oxidation and liver disease therapeutics
pmc-12586646.creator: Jong-Won Kim, Mengyun Ke, Donovan Whitfield, Bin Yang, Gu Seob Roh, Wen Xie
pmc-12586646.description: Cysteine (Cys) posttranslational modifications play a critical role in regulating protein function, cellular signaling and redox homeostasis in various physiological and pathological conditions. Sulfiredoxin-1 (SRXN1) has emerged as a key regulator of protein redox homeostasis through its involvement in Cys sulfinylation.

pmc-12652534.title: Evaluating the Impact of Regulatory Guidelines on Market Adoption and Implementation of Telehealth for COPD Patients: A Systematic Literature Review
pmc-12652534.creator: Noha Saeed Alghamdi, Nora Ann Colton, Paul Taylor, Grzegorz Bulaj
pmc-12652534.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Purpose: Telehealth (TH) offers promising solutions for enhancing the management of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), particularly in resource-limited or remote settings. However, regulatory uncertainty remains a significant barrier to adopting and integrating TH technologies into routine care. This systematic review aims to evaluate the role of regulatory guidelines in implementing and adopting TH solutions for COPD care and to identify key barriers and facilitators shaping these regulatory efforts.

pmc-13234188.title: The effect of Mauritanian and Benguela upwelling waters on micronekton (Decapoda, Euphausiacea, and Lophogastrida) in the Southeastern Atlantic Ocean
pmc-13234188.creator: Javier Díaz-Pérez, Heino Fock, Sabrina Duncan, Tim Dudeck, Santiago Hernández-León, José M Landeira
pmc-13234188.description: Eastern Boundary Upwelling Systems play a crucial role in marine productivity, supporting rich biodiversity and sustaining significant global fisheries. These dynamic regions are characterized by nutrient-rich waters that fuel complex food webs, making them vital for ecosystem functioning and fisheries management.

pmc-13388401.title: Spatial genetic mapping links shared inflammatory bowel disease liability to adult immune–epithelial lesion contexts
pmc-13388401.creator: Guangyi Tao, Hanzhe Du, Jun Zhao, Zhonghe Zeng, Junwu Cui, Longming Lei
pmc-13388401.description: BackgroundInflammatory bowel disease (IBD), including Crohn’s disease (CD) and ulcerative colitis (UC), shows marked clinical heterogeneity despite a shared immune-genetic background. The adult spatial contexts through which inherited IBD susceptibility is expressed remain unclear.MethodsWe integrated GWAS summary statistics for overall IBD, CD, and UC with LDSC, stratified LDSC, LDSC-SEG, MAGMA, PoPS, and genetically informed spatial mapping (gsMap).
